title: RFK Jr.'s embrace of AI confounds some MAHA allies and medical experts
source_used: ABC News (AP wire copy); apnews.com page blocked
key_facts: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. told a MAHA (Make America Healthy Again) summit that AI will free Americans from 'medical tyranny' by letting them fact-check their own medical advice.
Some MAHA allies, including Dr. Robert Malone, criticised the summit as 'pay-to-play'; sponsors paid up to $300,000.
OpenAI and Anthropic were among the sponsors, with more than a dozen other companies that have pending business before the government.
Bioethicist Zeke Emanuel said Kennedy 'obviously doesn't understand how AI works' because AI aggregates existing medical expertise.
HHS spokesperson Emily Hilliard said Emanuel described 'one narrow use' and that Kennedy wants AI to help people understand their health data and help doctors work faster.
Medicare officials have been in talks with several medical chatbot companies, including one behind a Utah program for AI-enabled prescription refills.
UCSF's Robert Wachter said AI adoption will likely reinforce professional recommendations; studies of real-time patient use found problems such as missing information and mixed advice.
quote_evidence: We're never ever again going to be able to be dominated by public officials who tell us: 'Trust the experts.'
He obviously doesn't understand how AI works.
why_it_matters_hint: The US health secretary is promoting AI as a patient tool, drawing criticism from both his own movement and medical experts.
event_date: MAHA summit held the week before 6 Oct 2026
notes: apnews.com returned 403; read the AP wire copy on ABC News. Summit date not stated precisely in the text ('last week').
